title: Security posture discovery with Silvercrest Finance
summary: Intro discovery focused on Silvercrest's compliance requirements and options between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Main concerns: SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and tenant separation, audit logs and SIEM integration, KMS/BYOK options, and data retention policies. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO reports, private deployment architecture, and schedule pilot benchmark with SE.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Send SOC2 and ISO27001 reports and summary (Jesse)
Share private deployment architecture doc + network diagram (Maya)
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run with sample prompts and latency targets (Maya/Ben)
Provide Dedicated pricing and committed capacity options (Jesse)
Follow-up call with procurement to review contract terms (Jesse/Tom)
action_items: Maya Chen: Share SOC2/ISO artifacts, redacted - include cert dates and scope (due 2026-05-22)
Maya Chen: Send private deployment whitepaper and VPC peering diagram (due 2026-05-21)
Jesse Park: Send Dedicated pricing options and contract summary (due 2026-05-20)
Ben Turner: Provide list of compliance stakeholders and expected retention windows (due 2026-05-24)
transcript:
Header:
Date: Tue May 19 2026 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ben Turner (CTO, Silvercrest), Aisha Rahman (Head of Security), Tom Keegan (Procurement)

[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Jesse Park, account exec at Redwood, and with me is Maya our solutions engineer. Appreciate you taking the time. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Ben: Yep Ben Turner, CTO at Silvercrest, we run a couple of ML services internally and evaluating vendors for generative features.
[00:18] Aisha: Aisha Rahman, Head of Security. I'll be focused on compliance, encryption, auditability.
[00:23] Tom: Tom Keegan, procurement, I'll be on contracting and timelines.
[00:28] Maya: Great, thanks. Agenda for today is to understand your security posture and requirements and talk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, especially around SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS.
[00:39] Ben: Perfect. Short context: we have sensitive PII and financial data in some prompts, we need strong controls, SOC2 or ISO is a hard requirement — preferably both.
[00:48] Aisha: Yep and we need to integrate with Okta for SSO, enterprise RBAC so devs can't access production keys, and logs shipped to our SIEM.
[00:56] Jesse: Totally, good starting list. Quick question on deployment preference — are you leaning Hosted or Dedicated/Private?
[01:05] Ben: Ideally hosted if controls are equivalent, but if we can't do BYOK or VPC peering, we'll need Dedicated or Private. Latency is less critical than data residency and key control.
[01:18] Maya: Understood. For Hosted we support SOC2 Type II and maintain certs — we can share the report after an NDA, and we also have ISO27001 for the control plane. For BYOK you mentioned — we offer KMS integrations and a BYOK flow for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has managed keys but we also have a customer-managed key option for certain enterprise accounts.
[01:39] Aisha: Can you clarify that? BYOK on Hosted sounds atypical. Do you mean envelope encryption where we manage the LM keys but you wrap with our KMS?
[01:48] Maya: Right, sorry transcription glitch — yes, envelope encryption model: Redwood can encrypt model artifacts and logs with our keys and wrap those with your KMS key (we support AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure). For full control we recommend Dedicated with VPC or Private where the control plane is customer-managed.
[02:05] Tom: For procurement we need to see SLA and proof that keys are not exportable. Also interested in HSM support — do you support HSM-backed keys?
[02:14] Maya: Yes, we integrate with HSM-backed KMS providers; we can accept keys backed by a cloud HSM, and for Private deployments you can bring your own HSM. We should include architecture notes in the doc.
[02:25] Ben: How about audit logs — can we stream immutable logs to our SIEM in real time? Also token-level logging is a concern.
[02:34] Maya: We provide per-request audit logs, including request metadata, who called which route, model version, latency, and token counts. Logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to Splunk/Datadog via our log forwarder. There's an event schema — we'll send the sample. Note sometimes the transcript generator will show KV cache as K-V cash, so apologies for noise.
[02:55] Aisha: And retention — by default how long do you keep raw prompts and responses? We might need 30-day or 90-day windows, with options to discard PII earlier.
[03:05] Jesse: Default for Hosted is 30 days of ephemeral logs for quality and abuse monitoring, but enterprise contracts can set retention or opt out. For Dedicated/Private we can disable logging of prompts entirely or keep them in your VPC storage with your retention policy.
[03:22] Aisha: Good. Two important items: can you redact PII before it leaves client systems? Also, is there a purge API to delete given keys or records?
[03:32] Maya: We have client-side suggestions for PII redaction libraries and also a server-side PII scrubber as an opt-in. We expose a purge/delete API for stored artifacts and keys, and for Private deployments you control the storage layer so you can enforce deletion. We'll include the purge API sample.
[03:47] Ben: On RBAC — role separation for dev, infra, and analytics teams is critical. We need least privilege, and want to ensure engineers can't call prod models without a release gate.
[03:58] Maya: Redwood Console supports RBAC with role templates — admin, engineer, auditor, etc. You can integrate with SAML/SCIM for group sync from Okta. We also support per-route tokens and route-level policies to prevent ad-hoc model calls.
[04:14] Aisha: Are audit logs tied to user identity from SSO? We want downstream correlation in SIEM.
[04:20] Maya: Yes, logs include the user id and external idp mapping if SSO is enabled. When you use SAML + SCIM, we sync group and user IDs so logs can be correlated.
[04:30] Tom: What's the difference practically between Dedicated and Private here? I guess Dedicated is Redwood-managed infra with reserved GPUs, Private is customer-managed control plane?
[04:40] Jesse: Exactly. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, VPC peering, and dedicated tenancy but control plane still runs with Redwood. Private gives you a deployable control plane (customer-managed) — we can run in your VPC or on-prem. Private is best for strict data residency and compliance.
[04:55] Ben: Does Private mean we host the model weights too? We prefer weights inside our network.
[05:01] Maya: In Private yes, model weights and KV caches remain in your environment. For Dedicated you can request storage in a specific region and we do not egress prompts to external networks.
[05:12] Aisha: Are there SOC2 scope differences — like is Private out of scope for Redwood's hosted SOC2?
[05:18] Maya: Good point — our SOC2 covers Redwood-hosted control plane and managed infra. For Private deployments, you'll have a separate responsibility matrix — we'll provide the shared responsibility doc and we can do audits or provide evidence for the parts we manage.
[05:32] Ben: SIEM integration — you mentioned logs to S3 or Splunk. Can you also stream to our Kafka cluster?
[05:39] Maya: We don't support direct Kafka ingestion out of the box yet, but log-forwarder can run in your environment and push into Kafka. Many customers deploy the forwarder in their VPC. We'll include an example.
[05:50] Aisha: Encryption in transit — are TLS 1.2 minimum? Forward secrecy?
[05:55] Maya: Yes, TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 supported, forward secrecy enabled, and mutual TLS is supported for private peering in Dedicated/Private.
[06:05] Tom: Contractually we need indemnities around data breaches and subprocessor lists. Is Redwood willing to share subprocessor list?
[06:13] Jesse: We maintain a subprocessor list we'll share; we also have standard breach notification windows in our enterprise contract. We'll have legal review on indemnities — we can send a contract redline-ready draft.
[06:25] Ben: Performance question for benchmarks — if we run our prompts what kind of latency SLAs can we expect on Dedicated?
[06:33] Maya: Depends on model and batch strategy; for smaller models we see 50-200ms p50 on Dedicated with optimized kernels; for larger models p50 may be higher. We'll run an in-context benchmark with your sample prompts and quantify latency and cost.
[06:46] Aisha: Monitoring — do you expose token-level cost attribution per team? We need chargeback capabilities.
[06:53] Maya: Yes, Console provides token-level cost breakdown per token per route, and you can tag requests with metadata so cost can be attributed to teams or product lines.
[07:03] Ben: How do you handle model rollouts and regressions? We need to be able to rollback if quality degrades.
[07:09] Jesse: We have rollout features (canary, A/B), automatic fallback policies, and quality monitoring tied to evals. We'll show those in a demo.
[07:18] Tom: On data retention again — if we want a 7-day retention only for production prompts, how is that enforced?
[07:24] Maya: It's configurable per route; retention policies apply at storage level. For Hosted we store logs in our managed storage for the contract window, for Dedicated we can set retention and also ship copies to your S3 where you control lifecycle rules.
[07:36] Aisha: Does Redwood ever use customer prompts for model training? This is a big blocker for some finance teams.
[07:43] Jesse: No, by default Redwood does not train models on customer prompts. For Hosted we have an explicit policy that customer data isn't used for model training. We'll provide the security FAQ.
[07:54] Ben: Ok — on compliance artifacts can you share SOC2 Type II scope and last audit date?
[07:59] Maya: We'll share the SOC2 report after an NDA and our ISO27001 certificate; they include the audit date and in-scope services.
[08:08] Aisha: Is there support for penetration testing? We may want to run a third-party pentest against the integration points.
[08:13] Maya: Yes, we support customer pentests; there's a request process and we can provide a test window and scope. For Hosted there are specific guidelines; for Dedicated/Private you have more freedom to test in your environment.
[08:27] Ben: Any limitations on bringing sensitive model weights for Private? Licensing from model providers could be a factor.
[08:34] Maya: Right, model licensing is a separate constraint. For many open models it's straightforward, but for some license-restricted models you may need direct agreements. We'll include notes on supported model licenses and quantization options.
[08:48] Tom: Timeline — procurement wants a 60 day window to onboard, run pilot, and decide. Is that feasible?
[08:55] Jesse: Yes, 60 days is doable for Dedicated pilot. Private might take longer depending on network approvals and on-prem hardware. We'll propose a plan: week 1-2 share docs & infra checklist, week 3 run a benchmark, weeks 4-6 pilot, week 8 sign.
[09:10] Aisha: One more: can we rotate keys nightly and is there an automated key rotation support?
[09:16] Maya: We support key rotation via KMS; for BYOK you rotate keys in your KMS and Redwood's envelope system handles new key wrapping. For Private you control rotation fully.
[09:27] Ben: Anything else on logging — do you provide WORM (write once read many) for audit logs?
[09:33] Maya: We can support immutable log stores for compliance use cases — e.g., send logs to S3 with object lock enabled. We'll include an example for legal holds.
[09:44] Jesse: Quick recap before we wrap: Maya will share SOC2/ISO artifacts, private deployment doc, and a log schema. I'll send Dedicated pricing and contract summary. We'll schedule a benchmark run — Maya, can you lead scheduling?
[09:58] Maya: Yep I'll reach out with a 2-hour window options and the benchmark checklist.
[10:05] Tom: Procurement will need the redline-friendly contract and subprocessors list.
[10:09] Jesse: We'll include that. Anything else?
[10:12] Aisha: Could you also include the dataflow diagram showing where PII may touch Redwood components? That helps our auditors.
[10:18] Maya: Absolutely, I'll include a detailed dataflow with ingress/egress points.
[10:22] Ben: Thanks all. Looking forward to the artifacts and the pilot.
[10:25] Jesse: Great, thanks everyone — next follow-up in a week unless scheduling the pilot sooner.

Notes / imperfect transcription: speaker labels occasionally merged (Maya/May), numbers transcribed as words in a few places, 'KV cache' appeared as 'K-V cash' in auto transcript.

Links referenced (to be sent): SOC2 report (link via NDA), ISO27001 cert, Private deployment whitepaper, Log schema sample (JSON), Dedicated pricing spreadsheet, Benchmark checklist.

End of call.
